sections.h2: Where is the Gratiot County Register of Deeds and what are its hours?
sections.html:
The office is in the Gratiot County Courthouse at 214 E Center Street, Ithaca, Michigan 48847, and answers at 989-875-5217. It is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The county posts one-off closures on the department page, such as a short midday closure on November 10, 2026.

The register is a constitutional office that records more than 200 types of documents, among them quit claim and warranty deeds, land contracts, mortgages, liens, releases and powers of attorney. Records date to the mid-1800s and every recorded paper is open to anyone during business hours. The same counter takes passport applications until 3:30 p.m. on weekdays, and staff ask callers to confirm availability first.

The office does not prepare documents or answer legal questions, so use an attorney or a title company for the deed itself. Public terminals in the lower level of the courthouse and at the Treasurer's office let you look up parcel information free of charge.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Gratiot County?
sections.html:
Every document costs $30 to record, whatever its length, and the county accepts cash, check or credit card. Transfer tax and a tax certificate are added where they apply. The fee schedule comes from MCL 600.2567.

Gratiot County Register of Deeds fee list
ServiceFee
Recording any deed, mortgage or instrument$30
Each extra instrument assigned or discharged$3
Tax certificate for a warranty deed or land contract$5
Real estate record copy$1 per page
Certification of a copy$5 per document plus $1 per page
Name search in the real estate record$0.50 per year, $5 minimum

Parcel research through the Treasurer is priced separately. A printout at the terminals is $1 per page, phone lookups are $3, and a hard copy of property tax and assessment research is $5 per parcel. Each online account receives one free parcel lookup, and later lookups on records under the same owner name are free as well.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax calculated in Gratiot County?
sections.html:
Transfer tax applies to the price of the property, rounded up to the next $500 of value. Gratiot County, like every Michigan county under 2,000,000 people, charges 55 cents per $500 under MCL 207.504, and the state adds $3.75 per $500 under MCL 207.525. Together that is $4.30 per $500 step.

A sale at $140,000 contains 280 steps of $500, so the state tax is $1,050.00, the county tax is $154.00, and the pair totals $1,204.00 before the $30 recording fee. A $140,001 price steps up to $140,500 and adds $4.30. The deed has to state the full value on its face or carry a value affidavit.

  • County exemptions are in MCL 207.505, state exemptions in MCL 207.526.
  • Deeds in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure are exempt from the state tax.
  • Transfers from a parent to a child, stepchild or grandchild are exempt from the state tax.
  • Corrective quitclaim deeds that confirm title already vested are exempt from both.

sections.h2: When do Gratiot County property taxes go delinquent?
sections.html:
Bills are sent on July 1 and December 1. Current-year taxes are payable to the township, city or village treasurer until March 1 of the next year, and after that they belong to the Gratiot County Treasurer, who will quote a payoff by phone.

The county lays out how unpaid years stack up. Taxes unpaid after March 1 are delinquent. A year later, on the following March 1, they are forfeited. On March 31 of the year after that they are foreclosed. In the county's published example, 2025 taxes reach forfeiture on March 1, 2027 and foreclosure on March 31, 2028. The 2026 online foreclosure auction was scheduled for August 7 through tax-sale.info.

  • Delinquent taxes can be paid online by card through Graphite, which adds 2.75% with a $1 minimum. American Express is not accepted.
  • Neither the county nor local treasurers answer for an escrow company that failed to pay a mortgaged property's tax.
  • Gratiot County joined a settlement over surplus proceeds from tax foreclosure auctions held between 2013 and 2020, and its claims deadline was July 16, 2026, which has passed.
  • Mailed payments should arrive before the deadline, because since December 24, 2025 the Postal Service postmarks the date an item is processed, not the date it was mailed.

sections.h2: Who must certify taxes before a deed is recorded in Gratiot County?
sections.html:
The County Treasurer's office issues a tax certificate before the register records a warranty deed, a deed with a covenant of warranty, a land contract, or an assignment of a land contract with a warranty clause. MCL 211.135 asks for proof that taxes were paid for the five years before the instrument and that no tax liens or tax titles stand against the land.

The fee is $5. A quitclaim deed with no covenant of warranty skips this step. Ask the Treasurer for the certificate during the closing window, and ask for payoff figures if any year is unpaid, because the register will not record the deed until the certificate exists.

sections.h2: What happens after a deed is recorded in Gratiot County?
sections.html:
Staff check each document against Michigan law before accepting it. A recorded document is numbered in order, time stamped, scanned in full and cross indexed, and the legal description plus the names of buyer and seller are entered into the search system. That index is what lets a title company trace a chain of ownership later.

The recording also feeds the rest of county government. Township and city offices, the Equalization Department and the Treasurer's office each learn of a sale first from the register, and they use it to prepare valuations for the next tax roll.

Once recorded, anyone can view or copy the deed. Staff add that reviewing a document against recording requirements before submitting it avoids delays.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Gratiot County itself?
sections.html:
Gratiot County sits in central Michigan, was organized in 1855, and takes its name from Captain Charles Gratiot. Ithaca is the county seat and Alma is the largest city. The county covers about 572 square miles, and its classical revival courthouse is on the National Register of Historic Places. The 212.8 MW Gratiot County Wind Project opened in June 2012, the largest wind installation in the state.

The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 41,190 residents, down 1.4% from the 2020 base. For 2020 to 2024 it reports a median owner-occupied home value of $147,500, an owner-occupied rate of 78.9%, median household income of $63,556 and median gross rent of $834. There are 16,211 housing units and 14,775 households.

At the median value, state and county transfer tax on a $147,500 sale comes to $1,268.50. Owners with a house that needs repairs or carries delinquent taxes can still sell it, but the tax certificate and payoff letter should be ordered first.

faqs.q: How much does the Gratiot County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: $30 per document regardless of the number of pages, plus transfer tax and a $5 tax certificate when they apply.

faqs.q: What are the Gratiot County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., at 214 E Center Street in Ithaca. Passport applications are accepted until 3:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Can I pay Gratiot County delinquent taxes by credit card?
faqs.a: Yes. Delinquent taxes can be paid online by card through Graphite, which charges 2.75% with a $1 minimum and does not take American Express.

faqs.q: Does the Gratiot County register prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office does not prepare documents or answer legal questions, so use an attorney or title company, and review the document against recording requirements before submitting it.

faqs.q: When are Gratiot County property tax bills mailed?
faqs.a: July 1 and December 1. Contact the local township, city or village treasurer if a bill does not arrive.
